en.caution: The November selloff highlights two real structural debates beyond short-term market noise. First, Microsoft's capex is surging past $50 billion per quarter—pushing Q1 FY27 free cash flow down 27%—while third-party GPU delivery slips show it still depends on constrained external AI supply chains. Second, Anthropic's Claude Sheets and Meetings illustrate how autonomous AI agents could pressure per-seat Microsoft 365 renewals over time. Technically, breaking below the EMA 50 and EMA 100 on heavy volume signals caution; a sustained breach of the EMA 200 at $471.42 would mark a deeper trend shift.
cons: Free cash flow fell 27% year-over-year to $18.63 billion in Q1 FY27 as capex reached $45.2 billion and is guided above $50 billion in Q2.
Anthropic's November 10 rollout of Claude Sheets and Claude Meetings stoked investor fears that AI agents could erode per-seat Microsoft 365 revenue.
A global Microsoft 365 outage lasting roughly 24 hours on November 12–13 disrupted Outlook, Teams, and Copilot across businesses and governments.
Third-party GPU and neocloud capacity delivery delays constrained near-term Azure compute supply, pushing some expansion into calendar 2027.
en.fundamental: Microsoft sits at the enterprise layer of the AI value chain, monetizing both cloud compute and workplace software. Its Q1 FY27 report on October 28, 2026 confirmed robust demand: total revenue rose 19% year-over-year to $92.3 billion, operating income climbed 21% to $45.9 billion (49.7% margin), and GAAP EPS increased 32% to $4.92 ($4.89 non-GAAP). Disclosing Azure in dollars for the first time, Microsoft reported 48% growth to $33.2 billion, guided Q2 Azure to 49%–50%, and posted $677 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations (+73%). At Ignite on November 17, Microsoft reinforced its switching-cost moat with Agent 365 governance, Azure AI Gateway multi-model routing, custom Cobalt 200 Arm chips, and lower-cost MAI Code 2 models. The core trade-off is capital intensity: capex hit $45.2 billion, is guided above $50 billion in Q2, and compressed free cash flow 27% to $18.63 billion.
en.headline: Strong Azure 48% growth collides with high-volume selloff and AI-seat fears
news: Oct 28, 2026: Microsoft beat Q1 FY27 expectations with $92.3 billion in revenue (+19%) and $33.2 billion in Azure sales (+48%), while guiding Q2 Azure growth to 49%–50% and capex above $50 billion after third-party GPU capacity deliveries slipped.

Nov 10, 2026: Anthropic launched Claude Sheets (beta), Claude Meetings, and Claude Whiteboards targeting workplace productivity, triggering a 2.2% drop in MSFT and wider software seat-compression fears; Microsoft separately committed $1 billion to Anthropic's $26 billion IPO-linked private placement.

Nov 12–16, 2026: A roughly 24-hour global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, and Copilot for enterprises and governments. On November 16, Microsoft traced the failure to a latent July 2026 gateway lock-contention bug amplified by reduced capacity and a Teams failover.

Nov 17–20, 2026: At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Microsoft launched in-house MAI Code 2 and Decision 1.1 models as lower-cost alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic, alongside generally available Azure Cobalt 200 custom Arm VMs, Azure AI Gateway, Copilot Workspaces, and Agent 365.

Nov 18–20, 2026: Despite MSFT sliding to $484.52 on November 20 with volume 57% above average, major Wall Street brokerages including Morgan Stanley, RBC Capital, Bank of America, Jefferies, Stifel, and TD Cowen maintained positive ratings centered on Azure's backlog.
en.opportunity: For long-term AI infrastructure investors, the 13.3% pullback from $559.15 separates sentiment swings from hard enterprise demand. Commercial backlog jumped 73% to $677 billion, Azure is accelerating toward 49%–50% growth, and Ignite 2026 strengthened Microsoft's switching-cost moat by turning Copilot, Agent 365, and Azure AI Gateway into a multi-model control plane where customers can run MAI, OpenAI, or Anthropic models on Azure. Custom Cobalt 200 silicon and in-house MAI models also improve long-run inference margins. Technically, approaching the EMA 200 ($471.42) with RSI 14 near oversold (34.76) creates a closely watched stabilization zone.
en.opportunityCheck: The page's AI-opportunity profile looks largely sound, but AI revenue exposure now appears understated and should move higher. On October 28, Microsoft disclosed Azure surging 48% to $33.2 billion, Microsoft Cloud hitting $63.9 billion, Foundry revenue tripling sequentially, and commercial backlog reaching $677 billion—showing AI is already a primary growth engine. Keeping bottleneck and pricing power restrained still makes sense, however, as third-party GPU delivery delays highlighted supply reliance and Anthropic's new office tools test per-seat Microsoft 365 pricing. Optionality remains well supported by Cobalt 200 silicon and MAI models.
pros: Azure revenue accelerated 48% year-over-year to $33.2 billion in Q1 FY27 (October 28), with Q2 guidance raised to 49%–50% constant currency.
Commercial remaining performance obligations jumped 73% year-over-year to $677 billion, underscoring deep multi-year enterprise cloud commitments.
Operating income grew 21% to $45.9 billion (49.7% margin), proving Microsoft still protects profitability amid massive AI infrastructure investment.
Ignite 2026 (November 17) expanded lock-in and cost control via custom Cobalt 200 chips, in-house MAI Code 2 models, and Agent 365 governance.
risks: AI capex exceeding $50 billion per quarter could keep free cash flow depressed if enterprise AI monetization scales slower than depreciation.
AI-native workplace rivals such as Anthropic's Claude productivity suite could curb Microsoft 365 seat growth or pricing power.
Recurring third-party GPU and data-center capacity bottlenecks could delay Azure revenue conversion into calendar 2027.
High-profile cloud reliability incidents like the November 12–13 Microsoft 365 outage and ongoing FTC/EU cloud-licensing probes could add enterprise friction.
en.summary: Microsoft (MSFT) shares dropped 13.3% from their $559.15 52-week high to $484.52 on November 20, 2026, sliding below key moving averages on heavy selling volume. The pullback contrasts sharply with strong Q1 FY27 results on October 28, where revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion, Azure jumped 48% to $33.2 billion, and commercial backlog surged 73% to $677 billion. Near-term pressure reflects Anthropic's November 10 launch of Claude Sheets and Meetings, a 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage on November 12–13, and investor concern over $50 billion+ quarterly AI capital spending.
en.technical: MSFT shows a bearish short-to-medium-term breakdown as of November 20, 2026, closing down 2.77% at $484.52. On trend, the three Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs — trend lines tracking average price over 50, 100, and 200 days) remain bullishly stacked at $513.60, $493.23, and $471.42, yet price has sliced beneath both the EMA 50 and EMA 100. That leaves the EMA 200 ($471.42) as critical long-term support, with $493–$514 now acting as overhead resistance. Momentum confirms downside control: MACD (a trend-momentum gauge comparing two moving averages) sits deeply negative at -6.05 versus its -0.77 signal line, producing a widening -5.27 histogram. RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge; under 30 is oversold) stands at 34.76—weak and nearing oversold, though not yet signaling exhaustion. On volatility, closing below the lower Bollinger Band (a 20-day volatility envelope from $491.18 to $554.73, middle $522.96) flags stretched near-term selling. Price now sits 13.3% off its $559.15 52-week high and at 64.5% of its $349.20–$559.15 range. Volume of 47.12 million shares—57% above the 30.00 million 20-day average—confirms institutional distribution rather than thin drift.

cons: กระแสเงินสดอิสระ Q1 FY27 ลดลง 27% YoY เหลือ $18.63 พันล้าน จาก CapEx ที่สูงถึง $45.2 พันล้าน และคาดเกิน $50 พันล้านใน Q2
การเปิดตัว Claude Sheets และ Claude Meetings ของ Anthropic วันที่ 10 พ.ย. จุดกระแสกังวลว่า AI Agent จะกดดันยอดไลเซนส์รายหัว Microsoft 365

th.fundamental: Microsoft ยืนอยู่ชั้นซอฟต์แวร์และคลาวด์องค์กรของห่วงโซ่ AI ทำรายได้ทั้งจากโครงสร้างพื้นฐานคลาวด์และชุดซอฟต์แวร์ทำงาน งบ Q1 FY27 วันที่ 28 ต.ค. 2026 ยืนยันความต้องการแกร่ง รายได้รวมโต 19% YoY แตะ $92.3 พันล้าน กำไรจากการดำเนินงานโต 21% ที่ $45.9 พันล้าน (มาร์จิ้น 49.7%) และ GAAP EPS โต 32% ที่ $4.92 (Non-GAAP $4.89) โดยเปิดเผยตัวเลข Azure เป็นดอลลาร์ครั้งแรกที่ $33.2 พันล้าน (+48%) พร้อมคาดการณ์ Q2 โต 49%–50% และมียอดสัญญาค้างรับองค์กร (RPO) พุ่ง 73% แตะ $677 พันล้าน ในงาน Ignite 17 พ.ย. บริษัทยังเสริมเกราะ switching costs ด้วย Agent 365, Azure AI Gateway, ชิป Arm Cobalt 200 และโมเดล MAI Code 2 ที่ต้นทุนต่ำกว่า แลกกับการใช้ทุนมหาศาลที่ CapEx แตะ $45.2 พันล้านและคาดทะลุ $50 พันล้านใน Q2 จนกดกระแสเงินสดอิสระลง 27% เหลือ $18.63 พันล้าน
th.headline: Azure โตแรง 48% สวนทางแรงขายวอลุ่มหนาและกระแสกังวลซอฟต์แวร์ AI
news: 28 ต.ค. 2026: Microsoft รายงานงบ Q1 FY27 ดีกว่าคาดด้วยรายได้ $92.3 พันล้าน (+19%) และ Azure $33.2 พันล้าน (+48%) พร้อมให้กรอบ Q2 Azure โต 49%–50% และ CapEx เกิน $50 พันล้านหลังการส่งมอบกำลัง GPU จากคู่ค้าล่าช้า
